title: Efficient Full-Context Retrieval for Long Documents

contributions.purpose: Enable efficient sentence-level retrieval for long-document QA without the chunking of RAG (which loses global context) or the quadratic cost of transformer full-context processing.
contributions.mechanism: Mamba retriever 130M and 1.3B: adapt the Mamba-2 state-space model into a fine-grained sentence-level retriever by removing the LM head, adding a classification head, and labeling the last token of each sentence for relevance to a prepended query; processes the entire document in linear time using all preceding context.
contributions.evaluation: Outperforms state-of-the-art embedding models (e.g. NV-Embed-v2-7B) across 41 long-document Q&A benchmarks (Table 1) with fewer FLOPS and faster processing (Table 2); on documents >256k tokens reaches performance close to GPT-4o full-context while using ~160x fewer tokens (avg 1,600 tokens selected).
contributions.source_quote: The Mamba retriever is the first successful transformation of a state-space model (Dao & Gu,2024) into a fine-grained, sentence-level retriever for RAG pipelines. It outperforms state-of-the-art em-bedding models across 41 long-document Q&A benchmarks (see Table 1).

contributions.purpose: Produce training data with sentence-level relevance labels that teach retrievers to leverage long-range document connections, since long documents lack such labels.
contributions.mechanism: Novel link-based synthetic data generation: an LLM discovers real connections between chunks in a document (from an initial chunk plus surrounding context) and transforms them into coherent questions requiring information from distinct parts of the document, labeling relevant sentences.
contributions.evaluation: Training 130M Mamba retrievers on 500k synthetic questions under identical conditions, the link-based strategy achieves the strongest results vs chunk-based and pair-based baselines (Table 4); pair-based strongly underperforms due to flawed questions.
contributions.source_quote: A key contribution of this paper is our novel link-based synthetic data generation method, which discovers real connections within a document and transforms these connections into coherent and realistic questions that require using different parts of the document to answer.

contributions.purpose: Validate that the link-based synthetic data method is responsible for the retriever's ability to capture long-range dependencies.
contributions.mechanism: Controlled comparison training identical 130M retrievers on synthetic data from the three strategies (chunk-based, pair-based, link-based) generated from the same documents.
contributions.evaluation: Link-based generation yields the best downstream retrieval (Table 4); qualitative case studies show Mamba retriever captures cross-sentence contextual relationships that NV-Embed-v2-7B misses despite high semantic similarity.
contributions.source_quote: We further demonstrate the effectiveness of our link-based method over baseline synthetic data methods.

self_declared_provenance.quote: Some recent works turn SSMs into embedding models (Hwang et al., 2024; Zhang et al., 2024a). In particular, Saad-Falcon et al. (2024) built a retrieval embedding model from the Monarch Mixer architecture (Fu et al., 2024). This line of work is tangential to our paper because we formulate Mamba retriever as a sentence-level retriever and not an embedding model.

Embedding Models NV-Embed-v2-7B(Lee et al., 2024), GTE-Qwen2 ... excel at identifying semantically simi-lar sentences within localized contexts ... However, sentence-level retrieval in long-context tasks requires a more comprehensive approach that needs a global understanding of the entire document. Our proposed Mamba retriever can naturally process the full document and perform sentence-level retrieval based on the global understanding of the document.

The Mamba retriever is built using the Mamba-2 architecture (Dao & Gu, 2024) ... Starting with a pretrained Mamba-2 checkpoint, we remove the language modeling head and replace it with a classification head.

notes: Explicit limitation stated by authors: synthetic data generation is expensive - more than $1000 for one million examples - and finding cheaper high-quality data methods is left to future work. Sparse-attention baselines (Longformer/LongT5) are noted to achieve linear scaling 'at the expense of some performance degradation.' Code, datasets, and checkpoints are released (resource contribution alongside method). Paper was rejected.
